items.title: Chil4 regulates basal cell activation and neuronal differentiation in olfactory epithelium regeneration
items.author: Yiqun Yu
items.content: Chil4 regulates horizontal basal cell activation, sensory neuronal and sustentacular cell differentiation, and inflammatory cell recruitment in the olfactory epithelium post injury, revealing a complex mechanism underlying olfactory epithelium regeneration.

items.title: MAPK drives UGTs metabolic resistance to neonicotinoids in whitefly by regulating the transcription factor HR39
items.author: Youjun Zhang
items.content: P38/ERK-HR39 signaling activates BtUGT356B1 transcription to directly metabolize neonicotinoids in whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci), revealing a key insect metabolic resistance regulatory axis.

items.title: Independently modulated genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae TIGR4 reveal transcriptional rewiring in antibiotic-adapted and antibiotic-sensitive strains
items.author: Shigetada Kawabata
items.content: iModulon analysis is applied to Streptococcus pneumoniae TIGR4 RNA-seq data. Independently modulated genes reveal transcriptional rewiring in antibiotic-adapted and antibiotic-sensitive strains, providing a scalable, interpretable framework.

items.title: pH-responsive hyaluronic acid nanocarrier activates cGAS/STING-mediated immunotherapy in colorectal cancer
items.author: Haili Wu
items.content: A hyaluronic acid-modified pH-sensitive liposome enables targeted delivery of kaempferol for colorectal cancer therapy. The formulation improves kaempferol stability, cellular uptake, and antitumor activity while promoting antitumor immune responses.

items.title: The KH-like CTD of Prp5 is conserved and essential for splicing
items.author: Sittinan Chanarat
items.content: The C-terminal domain of the yeast splicing helicase Prp5 is essential for cell survival and, despite resembling a KH-like RNA-binding fold, it actually interacts with the key spliceosomal protein Hsh155.

items.title: Dynamic fate of beige adipocytes in fat grafting and inflammatory regulation
items.author: Tong Liu
items.content: Whether beige adipocytes generated during fat grafting help or harm graft survival was studied using cell culture, mouse tracing models, and immune modulation. The study showed that browning is an adaptive response and that beige adipocytes can revert to white adipocytes without dedifferentiating.
